morgan: Quick check — PR ready but need to confirm auth header precedence and rotation policy for tests. If a request contains both `Authorization: Bearer ...` and `X-API-Key: ...`, which takes precedence? Also what's the expected behavior during key rotation (how long do we accept old key)? Example headers:
```
Authorization: Bearer abc123
X-API-Key: svc-987
X-Project-ID: proj-42
```
I'm adding unit tests around: header precedence, project scoping when both headers present, and mapping invalid/missing -> 401 vs 403.

jia: Precedence is: if a valid `Authorization` bearer token is present, we treat request as the user token (Authorization wins). If no Authorization, we fall back to `X-API-Key`. That was changed in https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal/commit/... :thumbsup:

sam: Add note on project/org scoping: If `X-Project-ID` is provided we authorize against the API key's accessible projects. If Authorization token is present, project lookup is done via token claims unless `X-Project-ID` is an explicit override (we only allow override for service keys, not user tokens). So with both Authorization + X-API-Key + X-Project-ID, we treat as user token + ignore project override. 

alex: Also make sure the SDK fallback behavior is explicit. Current `node-sdk` will set `X-API-Key` when `apiKey` config is used. We should NOT auto-inject `Authorization` from apiKey. If both headers surface from client config that's on the app to resolve. For compatibility: prefer Authorization server-side but log a warning (non-blocking) when both present so we can surface to customers.

sam: Mapping guidance: 401 = auth missing/invalid (no matching creds), 403 = auth valid but forbidden (no access to requested project/route). E.g. invalid API key -> 401, valid key but project mismatch -> 403.

deploy-bot: Reminder: scheduled key rotation for service pool `svc-default` at 2026-04-02T03:00Z. Old keys accepted for 15m grace window. See https://infra.redwood/schedules/rotations :rotating_light:

morgan: OK I'll update the PR to implement precedence (Authorization > X-API-Key), add tests for project override behavior and 401/403 mapping, and include a note about the 15m grace. Ping @jia and @alex for review when ready.

jia: Sounds good — I'll review after standup.

alex: quick nit: add an integration test that exercises a request with both headers and a project override to ensure we ignore the override for user tokens.

morgan: will do, thanks everyone :raised_hands:
